notes:
Apple Music, found in Sorriva and played by your speakers.

SEARCH APPLE'S WHOLE CATALOGUE. Discover is now a search box over every album Apple sells — no Apple Music account, no sign-in, nothing to set up. Open an album and you get its cover, year, label and full track listing.

PLAY IT ON ANY ZONE. Pick a zone and it plays. Your speakers fetch the music straight from Apple, so the phone is never carrying the audio — lock it, walk away, let the battery die, and the music keeps going. That is the same property your NAS library has and no streaming source in Sorriva has had before.

IT KNOWS WHAT IT IS PLAYING. Track, artist, album, cover art and the track length, and it stays right when you skip. Zone cards now show the album name.

APPLE MUSIC APPEARS IN SERVICES. Sorriva asks your speakers what your household actually has rather than guessing, and shows Apple Music as connected when it is there — with the one remaining step spelled out if there is one. It has left the Coming Soon list.

DISCOVER IS NOW ABOUT DISCOVERY. It was a placeholder promising AI. It is the home for finding music you do not own, whichever way you find it — AI included, later.

NOT IN THIS RELEASE, and it is a proof rather than a finished feature: nothing is saved. There is no way yet to keep an album, put Apple music in your library alongside your FLAC, play a single track, build a playlist, or browse by artist. Those are the next pieces, in that order.
